title: Meta Descriptions: How to Write Them | AMK Digital Agency
description: How Google chooses the snippet under a result, when it uses your meta description, and how to write unique descriptions that help people choose.

article.summary: The meta description can become the short text under your result. Learn when Google uses it and how to write one that helps people decide to click.
article.author: AMK Digital Agency
takeaways: Google mainly builds snippets from the page content, and uses your meta description when it describes the page better.
There is no length limit; long descriptions are shortened to fit the screen.
Write a unique description for each important page, starting with your key pages.

blocks.text: Meta descriptions: what they do and how to write them

blocks.html: A meta description is a short summary inside the page's code: <meta name="description" content="…">. Visitors do not see it on the page itself, but search engines can show it as the snippet under your result.

Google creates snippets automatically. The page's own content is the main source. Google may use the meta description instead when it gives a better summary of the page than the text on the page does.

blocks.caption: Where the snippet comes from
rows: The meta description accurately summarises the page
The meta description is vague or repeated on many pages
The search is about one specific detail on the page
The part of the page that matches the search

blocks.html: There is no limit on how long a meta description can be. In results, snippets are shortened as needed, usually to fit the device width. Keep the most useful information at the start so it is still visible after shortening.

blocks.text: How to write a good meta description

items.title: Summarise the page honestly
items.html: Say what the visitor will find: the topic, the format and who it is for.

items.title: Include useful specifics
items.html: Facts such as a price range, opening hours, a product's key feature or the steps covered.

items.title: Make it unique
items.html: Avoid one generic description copied across many pages. If you have many pages, start with the most important ones.

items.title: Read it as a searcher
items.html: Would this sentence help you choose between results?

blocks.html: If a site has thousands of similar pages, such as product pages, descriptions can often be generated from each page's own data (name, key details, price) so every one is different and accurate.

items: The same description on many pages
A list of keywords instead of a sentence
A description that does not match the page
No description on the most important pages

blocks.html: Check any page with our free Meta Tag Analyser: it shows the description, its length and a search result preview.

blocks.question: Will Google always show my meta description?
blocks.answer: No. Google chooses the snippet for each search and may use text from the page instead, especially when the search is about a specific detail.
